doc.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Technique versus ideas
summary: Davern says technique only executes an idea and one well-placed note beats many.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: You’ve got to have some though.
Technique is only good enough to execute an idea. If you have no ideas, then technique by itself is not music.

It’s not even that. It’s not as good as that. An etude at least has form and shape. But technique, how many notes you can cram into a bar is totally meaningless. One note, well placed at the right time with the right intensity, is worth more than a thousand notes played at a velocity that’s like fancy footwork, it’s dazzling. It’s good for children. Children like to be dazzled. But mature people don’t want to be dazzled, only unless it’s to show a point or say, see I can do that too. Yeah, but technique is really nothing more than the execution of an idea. If you have no ideas, then you’re just an array of cunning stunts.
